fr3._note: Derived from training_eligsir.json frame 75/225 (img_name=1341847980... actually 1341848009.878688), a real captured camera pose ~1/3 into the trajectory. Look-ahead distance 4.0m (clipped from scene bbox diagonal), camera position pulled back an additional 55% of that distance (2.2m) beyond the real pose for more context (iteration 2: supervisor feedback said the first pass -- 30% pullback -- was still a touch too tight; increased to 55%.) Target unchanged from the original derivation. Position/target rotated 180deg about Z ((x,y,z)->(-x,-y,z)) to match the fixed entity.setLocalEulerAngles(0,0,180) every gsplat entity gets in this viewer's loader (world up is -Y in the raw trajectory frame; this flip converts to the +Y-up the fixed-roll viewer camera assumes -- verified via mean camera 'down' vector per scene).

kitchen1._note: Derived from training_eligsir.json frame 68/204 (img_name=000689), a real captured camera pose ~1/3 into the trajectory. Position pulled back ~30% beyond that pose along its view direction for context (look distance 2.49m derived from the scene's bbox diagonal in scene_bounds.json, clipped to [1.5, 4.0]m). Both position and target are then rotated 180deg about Z ((x,y,z) -> (-x,-y,z)) to match the fixed entity.setLocalEulerAngles(0,0,180) applied to every gsplat entity by this viewer's loader (office.html:94227) -- the source camera-trajectory export is in the reconstruction's raw camera-initialized frame (verified: mean camera 'down' vector for every scene is ~(0,+1,0), i.e. world up is -Y there, not the +Y the fixed-roll viewer camera assumes), and this same 180deg-about-Z flip is what the shipped office.html example relies on to render right-side up, so applying it here keeps the camera consistent with the splat geometry's actual on-screen orientation without needing a separate up-vector override (the viewer's camera schema has no explicit 'up' field).
